LESSON: WRITING 3.3.1 SEQUENCING IDEAS

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.3: Writing 3.3.1 Sequencing Ideas
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 3.3.1 Sequencing Ideas, part of Strand 3 in Grade 5 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: when using a vehicle) on the theme, 1. How can you ensure your ideas flow in communication? 2. Why do we use connectors in writing?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify connectors in texts for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 3.3.1 Sequencing Ideas in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use connectors to sequence ideas logically in a paragraph for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 3.3.1 Sequencing Ideas in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. enjoy writing texts using connectors for effective communication.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 3.3.1 Sequencing Ideas in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify connectors in texts for effective communication,

   Writing 3.3.1 Sequencing Ideas helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. use connectors to sequence ideas logically in a paragraph for comprehension,

   Writing 3.3.1 Sequencing Ideas helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. enjoy writing texts using connectors for effective communication.

   Writing 3.3.1 Sequencing Ideas helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 3.3.1 Sequencing Ideas together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to learn: This is enhanced as the learner interacts with content when searching for various connectors used in

writing.

• Critical thinking and Problem solving: This is enhanced as the learner follows simple instructions to connect sentence

strips to form a paragraph using appropriate connectors.

Values:
• Love: This is enhanced as the learner portrays a caring attitude when sharing ideas with peers as they search for various

sentence connectors.

• Social justice: This is promoted as the learner fosters inclusivity of ideas and gives honest feedback to peers during peer

review.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)):

Safety and security: This is enhanced as learner gets knowledge on prevention and possible triggers of road accidents.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of paragraph writing to their learning of similar concepts in English.
